title: Learning from waste: Machine Learning for health risk prediction and computer vision-based sorting in Ghana
abstract: arXiv:2608.25759v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The inappropriate disposal of solid waste remains a significant public health and environmental concern worldwide, including in Ghana. Poor sanitation and improper waste management practices contribute to substantial economic costs and avoidable deaths annually. In 2022, a field study in Atonsu, Kumasi, Ghana, reported a community-perceived relationship between household waste disposal and illness patterns, but only through descriptive analysis without quantitative validation. This study extends that investigation using two data-driven approaches. First, a Random Forest classifier was developed to predict illness categories using waste disposal practices and demographic survey data. On a held-out group of respondents who reported illness (N=69), the model obtained a macro F1 score of 0.63, with disposal method emerging as the most important substantive predictor of illness type. translated_title: 从废弃物中学习：机器学习在加纳健康风险预测和基于计算机视觉的垃圾分类中的应用
translated_abstract: 固体废物的不当处置仍然是全球范围内，包括加纳在内的重要公共卫生和环境问题。卫生条件差和废物管理实践不当每年导致大量经济损失和可避免的死亡。2022年，在加纳库马西阿通苏进行的一项实地研究报告了社区感知到的家庭废物处置与疾病模式之间的关系，但仅通过描述性分析，没有进行定量验证。本研究通过两种数据驱动方法扩展了这一调查。首先，开发了一个随机森林分类器，利用废物处置实践和人口统计调查数据预测疾病类别。在报告患病的受访者保留组（N=69）中，模型获得了0.63的宏F1分数，其中处置方法成为疾病类型最重要的实质性预测因子。其次，一个MobileNetV2图像分类模型实现了自动化的废物分类。
tldr: 本研究利用随机森林分类器预测疾病类型（宏F1分数0.63）和MobileNetV2图像模型进行废物分类，首次定量验证了加纳废物处置与疾病之间的关系。
en_tdlr: This study quantitatively validates the waste-illness relationship in Ghana using a Random Forest classifier (macro F1 0.63) and enables automated waste sorting via MobileNetV2 image classification.
